name: cohuleen druith

attributes.attribute: lost the cap, then stayed landbound
known also as cohullen, from the Irish cochall, a hood
alternate name for the cap-wearing water-maidens of Ireland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The cohuleen druith belongs to Irish folklore. The name runs also as cohullen, from the Irish cochall, a hood. Storytellers gave this magical hood or cap to the mermaids and merrows of Ireland. The cap showed red and carried a covering of feathers. It let its wearer pass below the waves and live under the sea. If a person stole the cap, the mermaid could not go back beneath the water. She then had to stay landbound, cut off from her home beneath the sea.

okr.objective: The cohuleen druith is the Irish cap that lets a mermaid live beneath the waves.
key_results: The name runs also as cohullen, from the Irish cochall, a hood.
Mermaids and merrows wore this red cap covered with feathers.
